title: Field transfer of Hydrosheaf under data scarcity: robustness, uncertainty and limits across three Ghanaian groundwater datasets
scope: Field transfer and robustness benchmark of the identifiability-aware Hydrosheaf reaction-inference workflow, applied unchanged to one well-resourced and two sparse Ghanaian groundwater datasets; evaluates transferability and honesty of reporting, not independent validation of reactions, flow paths or ages.

objectives.statement: Dataset readiness: what can and cannot be inferred from each Ghanaian dataset given its available evidence tier.
acceptance_criteria: Per-dataset tier attainment and missingness quantified
Independent charge-balance audit classifies quality tiers per dataset (no external quality-class field exists in the canonical raw data to check it against)

objectives.statement: Field transfer: how stable are reaction-class support, evidence gates and identifiability class across season and administrative region in Northern Ghana (no independent aquifer-type classification exists for these boreholes).
Diagnostic robustness: how much do process labels, reaction-class confidence and identifiability class change when diagnostics are removed.
acceptance_criteria: Gate on/off and synthetic-truth validation completed

objectives.statement: Connectivity robustness: do conclusions depend too strongly on assumed edges.
External transfer: what transfers, and what are the failure modes, when the workflow is applied to genuinely sparse external datasets.
acceptance_criteria: Talensi and Lower Anayari evaluated at native tier against matched-tier Northern Ghana references

objectives.statement: Limits: which process classes are identifiable, weakly identifiable, or non-identifiable under field data scarcity.

inputs.provenance: Northern Ghana seasonal groundwater chemistry workbook, canonical raw Dry/Wet sheets only (320 samples, 160 wells, March/August 2025). An earlier revision additionally read data/NorthenGhana/Aquifers_Dataset_Mendeley.xlsx, a different, antecedent study's own derived product (aquifer/geology/lithology metadata, workbook saturation indices, a provided graph-edge sheet, inferred process labels); that workbook is not this project's field data and has been removed entirely (DECISIONS.md).
Talensi artisanal-mining-area groundwater chemistry dataset (63 samples)
Lower Anayari groundwater chemistry dataset (41 samples)

risks.risk: Inferred labels from a different, antecedent study's derived workbook (Dominant_Process, Aquifer_Evolution_Label, Graph_Edges) could be mistaken for independent ground truth.
risks.mitigation: That workbook and its fields have been removed from this study entirely rather than retained as a concordance reference; honesty boundary stated in Methods, Study design, Discussion and DECISIONS.md.

risks.risk: Evidence-lift gate could manufacture apparent identifiability loss (circularity).
risks.mitigation: Gate on/off comparison and gate-independent structural diagnostics reported (Supplementary Methods S7, Extended Data Fig. 3).
